questions.q: What mitigation does LTV Global use to resolve Risk #2 from the Chapter 1 risk register — ownership skew from a single integration user?
options: Deleting all Parts Order records older than one week
Owning Parts Order records through region/business-unit queues instead of a single Meridian integration user
Giving every dealer their own Salesforce org
Storing Parts Orders only in Snowflake, never in Salesforce
questions.explain: Queue-based ownership, structured per region and business unit, distributes Parts Order records across a structure Salesforce's sharing engine handles well, resolving the ownership-skew risk a single integration-user owner would create.

questions.q: Why is Equipment Asset's Serial_Number__c field marked as an indexed external ID?
options: Because external IDs are required on every custom object regardless of query pattern
Because the most common query pattern (finding equipment by serial number) needs to stay selective and fast as the object grows past millions of rows
Because it allows the field to be deleted without affecting related records
Because external ID fields are exempt from Salesforce's standard data types
questions.explain: An indexed external ID keeps the serial-number lookup — used constantly by Field Service, the dealer portal, and the nightly Meridian sync — selective, which is the difference between a query that stays fast at scale and one that silently degrades.

questions.q: What does LTV Global do with Parts Order records older than 24 months?
options: Nothing — they remain in the standard object indefinitely
They are permanently deleted with no retention
They are moved into a Big Object (Parts_Order_Archive__b) indexed on Account and order date
They are moved into LedgerPoint
questions.explain: Aged Parts Orders move into a Big Object archive, keeping the live object's working size manageable while still serving the rare case of needing older order history.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is unbounded growth of the live Parts Order object a risk even with good indexing and queue ownership in place?
options: Because indexing becomes illegal past a certain record count
Because every read- and write-path problem gets worse the more total data there is to search through, regardless of indexing
Because Big Objects cannot coexist with standard objects in the same org
Because queues can only hold a fixed maximum number of records
questions.explain: The lesson explains that total data volume compounds every read- and write-path problem over time, which is why archiving aged records — not just indexing and queue ownership — is still a necessary part of the strategy.

questions.q: What is the main point this lesson makes about the relationship between Lesson 6's risk register and Lesson 10's LDV strategy?
options: Lesson 10 introduces an entirely new, unrelated risk with no connection to Chapter 1
Lesson 10 gives Lesson 6's Risk #2 an actual mechanism and name (queue ownership) rather than restating it as a new discovery
Lesson 6's risks are retired and no longer relevant by the time Lesson 10 is reached
Lesson 10 contradicts Lesson 6's original risk assessment
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this as resolving, not restating, the earlier risk — Lesson 6 named the danger, and Lesson 10 supplies the specific mitigation mechanism.
